emb:L2016855163.model_family: U-Net with efficient channel attention (ECA) modules
emb:L2016855163.clinical_problem: fetal cerebellum segmentation for CNS assessment
emb:L2016855163.patient_population: fetuses in the second trimester of pregnancy
emb:L2016855163.model_description: Takes 2D fetal ultrasound images as input and outputs a segmentation mask of the fetal cerebellum, using a U-Net backbone with efficient channel attention modules that replace fully connected layers with shared-parameter 1D convolutions to reduce parameters. Trained on an in-house database (JSUAH-Cerebellum) of second-trimester fetal ultrasound images with Gaussian blur and random flipping augmentation, intended to automate a step in fetal CNS ultrasound evaluation.
emb:L2016855163.dataset_size: JSUAH-Cerebellum database of second-trimester fetal ultrasound images (exact case count not stated)
emb:L2016855163.headline_result: Mean Jaccard Score 86.01% and Dice Similarity Coefficient 91.35%, 2.86% and 3.73% higher than baseline U-Net
emb:L2016855163.study_design: technical development / retrospective segmentation accuracy study

emb:L2016903508.model_family: coarse-to-fine U-Net hand segmentation + stacking ensemble of five convolutional neural networks
emb:L2016903508.patient_population: children and adolescents undergoing hand radiography
emb:L2016903508.model_description: Takes a hand radiograph as input. A coarse-to-fine step (density-based clustering followed by a U-Net) segments and cleans the hand region, and the resulting clean hand image is passed to a stacking ensemble of five convolutional neural networks that outputs an estimated skeletal (bone) age. Evaluated on a mix of public and clinical hand radiograph datasets.
emb:L2016903508.dataset_size: public and clinical hand radiograph datasets (exact count not stated)
emb:L2016903508.headline_result: Mean absolute error of 5.42 months (males) and 5.98 months (females)

emb:L635772659.exclusion_reason: practical guideline for performing and interpreting fMRI in children; does not describe or evaluate an AI/ML model

emb:L2018154832.exclusion_reason: fMRI-based prediction of a transdiagnostic behavioral trait (social impairment score) in a research cohort; basic neuroscience research, not a diagnostic radiology application

emb:L2018034861.exclusion_reason: review of AI tools for ADHD diagnosis/treatment spanning symptoms, MRI and EEG; not focused on radiologic imaging AI

emb:L2017611739.exclusion_reason: machine learning prediction of uterine dehiscence in the pregnant mother using ultrasound and clinical features; adult (maternal), not pediatric/fetal, patient

emb:L2017611205.clinical_problem: interpretation of common thoracic diseases on pediatric chest radiographs
emb:L2017611205.patient_population: 9,125 pediatric chest radiograph studies from a major pediatric hospital in Vietnam (2020-2021)
emb:L2017611205.model_description: Releases VinDr-PCXR, a large open pediatric chest radiograph dataset of 9,125 studies, each manually annotated by an experienced pediatric radiologist for 36 critical findings and 15 diseases, with abnormal findings marked by bounding boxes. Split into a training set of 7,728 and a test set of 1,397 studies to support development of computer-aided diagnosis algorithms for pediatric chest radiograph interpretation, a task under-served relative to adult chest radiography due to a lack of annotated pediatric datasets.
emb:L2017611205.release_evidence: the dataset was ... made publicly available on https://physionet.org/

emb:L2017677578.exclusion_reason: porcine dietary/microbiome study; not human, not diagnostic imaging

emb:L2015853430.exclusion_reason: phonocardiography (heart sound) analysis; not diagnostic imaging

emb:L2021924158.exclusion_reason: general clinical review of pediatric heart murmur evaluation and management; AI/imaging mentioned only briefly as an emerging technology

emb:L2017166847.exclusion_reason: multivariate pattern classification of familial dyslexia risk from infant resting-state fMRI; basic neuroscience research, not a diagnostic radiology application

emb:L2017268426.model_family: neural network trained on expert- and community-scored examples
emb:L2017268426.clinical_problem: automated quality control of diffusion MRI scans
emb:L2017268426.patient_population: children and adolescents from the Healthy Brain Network (HBN) study (N=2,747)
emb:L2017268426.model_description: Curates and preprocesses diffusion MRI data from the Healthy Brain Network study (N=2,747) into a standardized, analysis-ready open resource, including denoising and correction for motion, susceptibility distortion, and eddy currents. A neural network, trained using a small expert-scored subset plus a larger community-scored set, automatically scores the quality of every scan, intended to replace manual visual quality review for large-scale pediatric brain imaging research.
emb:L2017268426.release_evidence: Preprocessed, analysis-ready data was made openly available
emb:L2017268426.headline_result: Neural network QC concordant with expert ratings on a held-out set (ROC-AUC = 0.947)

emb:L2017166020.exclusion_reason: machine learning prediction of future alcohol misuse from adolescent brain structure; behavioral-outcome neuroscience research, not a diagnostic radiology application

emb:L2016899000.model_family: atlas-guided registration and deep learning segmentation
emb:L2016899000.clinical_problem: fetal cardiovascular anomaly assessment (congenital aortic arch anomalies)
emb:L2016899000.patient_population: fetuses with normal hearts and with congenital aortic arch anomalies
emb:L2016899000.model_description: Presents the first 3D fetal cardiac MRI atlases of normal and abnormal (congenital aortic arch anomaly) fetal heart anatomy, built from black-blood T2-weighted fetal MRI reconstructed into 3D via slice-to-volume registration. Evaluates the feasibility of atlas-guided registration and deep learning methods for automated multi-label vessel segmentation from these images.

emb:L2016898915.model_family: deep learning label propagation combined with a 3D residual U-Net
emb:L2016898915.clinical_problem: prenatal diagnosis of congenital heart disease (coarctation of the aorta) via cardiac vessel segmentation
emb:L2016898915.patient_population: 40 fetuses with suspected coarctation of the aorta
emb:L2016898915.model_description: Takes T2-weighted black-blood fetal cardiac MRI as input and produces a multi-label segmentation of the fetal heart and great vessels. The network combines deep-learning label propagation from a multi-label anatomical atlas with a 3D residual U-Net, trained using single-label manual segmentations from routine clinical practice plus the atlas, to give more detailed anatomical labeling than the single-label approach for assessing coarctation of the aorta and other congenital heart disease.
emb:L2016898915.dataset_size: 40 fetal subjects with suspected coarctation of the aorta
emb:L2016898915.headline_result: Dice score 0.79 ± 0.02 for the fetal cardiac vessels region, statistically equivalent to a 3D residual U-Net trained solely on manual single-label data (p>0.05)
emb:L2016898915.study_design: retrospective technical development / segmentation accuracy study

emb:L2016843235.exclusion_reason: study population imaged in adulthood (adults born very preterm/very low birth weight); not a pediatric imaging population

emb:L2016898646.exclusion_reason: methodological/statistical paper on motion-related exclusion bias in resting-state fMRI research; not a diagnostic imaging model

emb:L2016898664.exclusion_reason: construction of a general-purpose functional brain network atlas/resource across a normal population; not a disease-specific diagnostic imaging tool

emb:L2018702682.model_family: multimodal MRI combined with machine learning (including brain-age prediction and imaging genetics)
emb:L2018702682.clinical_problem: understanding normal and atypical brain development in children with neurodevelopmental disorders
emb:L2018702682.model_description: A narrative review of 49 studies (1999-2021) summarizing multimodal structural, anatomical and functional MRI combined with machine learning techniques, including brain-age prediction and imaging genetics, used to map normal and atypical brain development in children. Discusses how these quantitative MRI/ML approaches may provide imaging biomarkers for earlier diagnosis, classification and prognosis of neurodevelopmental disorders.

emb:L2014360020.model_family: Faster R-CNN feature learning with an optimally-trained Recurrent Neural Network (Sun Flower Optimization)
emb:L2014360020.patient_population: children (hand radiographs collected manually and from public sources)
emb:L2014360020.model_description: Takes hand radiographs as input. The region of interest is segmented with adaptive Otsu thresholding, a Faster R-CNN learns features from the segmented region, and a recurrent neural network, whose training weights are tuned by a Sun Flower Optimization algorithm, uses those features to predict the child's Tanner-Whitehouse 3 bone age. Evaluated on a mix of manually collected and publicly available hand radiograph images.
emb:L2014360020.dataset_size: images collected manually and from public sources (exact count not stated)
emb:L2014360020.headline_result: superior performance compared to state-of-the-art bone age assessment techniques (no specific metric value given)

emb:L2014412037.model_family: functional/effective connectivity features (group ICA, dual regression, Granger causality) classified with WEKA classifiers
emb:L2014412037.patient_population: children, adolescents and adults, analyzed as separate age groups
emb:L2014412037.model_description: Uses resting-state fMRI to build a computer-aided diagnosis system for autism spectrum disorder. Group independent component analysis identifies resting-state networks, dual regression obtains individualized components, and functional (full/partial correlation) and effective (Granger causality) connectivity features are extracted between networks. Because connectivity differs by age, features and classifiers were selected separately for children, adolescent and adult groups and evaluated with a suite of classifiers to distinguish ASD from typically developing individuals.
emb:L2014412037.headline_result: 95.23% classification accuracy in the children age group using a classification-via-clustering classifier

emb:L2014515326.clinical_problem: prenatal detection of congenital heart defects via fetal echocardiography
emb:L2014515326.model_description: A review discussing the possibilities and limitations of applying artificial intelligence algorithms, including approaches adapted from adult cardiology, to fetal echocardiography in order to improve prenatal detection rates of congenital heart defects, which currently range from 22.5% to 52.8% in low-risk populations.

emb:L2017613102.exclusion_reason: review of cleft lip/palate orthodontic and surgical management; imaging use is dental/craniofacial orthodontic, an excluded imaging domain

emb:L2017672429.exclusion_reason: review of digital/AI techniques for oral disease diagnosis in children (intraoral photos, panoramic and cephalometric imaging); dental imaging, an excluded domain

emb:L2018484593.exclusion_reason: predicts a poorly defined behavioral 'aggression level' from MRI in children with a non-standard diagnosis (Deep OCD); not a diagnostic radiology application

emb:L2018662259.model_family: convolutional neural network for automated segmentation
emb:L2018662259.clinical_problem: fetal biometry (head circumference / biparietal diameter) for gestational age and growth assessment
emb:L2018662259.patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal ultrasound (110 labeled training images, 80 test images)
emb:L2018662259.model_description: Takes 2D fetal head ultrasound images as input and automatically segments the fetal head, fitting an ellipse by minimizing a cost function combining Dice score and ellipticity error, from which head circumference and biparietal diameter are calculated. Trained on 110 labeled images and tested on 80 ultrasound images, aiming to reduce the operator dependence and time cost of manual measurement.
emb:L2018662259.dataset_size: 110 labeled training images, 80 test ultrasound images
emb:L2018662259.headline_result: 94.31% success rate for HC/BPD measurement; 89.14% accuracy on plane acceptance check

emb:L2018683397.exclusion_reason: chest X-ray pneumonia classifier; pediatric mortality is cited only as background motivation and the dataset's pediatric status is not stated in the abstract

emb:L2018804153.exclusion_reason: chest X-ray pneumonia classifier; pediatric mortality is cited only as background motivation and the dataset's pediatric status is not stated in the abstract

emb:L2018876809.exclusion_reason: fNIRS (functional near-infrared spectroscopy) findings in ADHD pharmacotherapy; not a listed diagnostic radiology modality and no AI/ML model is developed or evaluated

emb:L2019670605.model_family: attention-based multiple-instance learning convolutional neural network
emb:L2019670605.clinical_problem: bone age assessment for endocrine, genetic and growth disorders
emb:L2019670605.model_description: Takes a whole hand radiograph, cropped into small patches, as input. A feature extraction network computes patch features, and an attention mechanism ranks and aggregates the patches by importance (multiple-instance learning) without requiring manual region-of-interest annotation; the aggregated image features are combined with sex to predict bone age, and the attention weights produce an interpretable heatmap of the regions used. Validated on the Radiological Society of North America 2017 pediatric bone age dataset.

emb:L2019706419.model_family: deep learning CNNs (GoogLeNet, VGG16_bn, VGG19_bn, ResNet18/34/50)
emb:L2019706419.clinical_problem: differentiating primary ciliary dyskinesia-related otitis media from simple otitis media with effusion
emb:L2019706419.patient_population: 31 children with primary ciliary dyskinesia and 30 age-matched children with otitis media with effusion
emb:L2019706419.model_description: Takes temporal bone CT images from children as input and classifies them as primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD)-related otitis media versus simple otitis media with effusion. Several deep learning architectures (GoogLeNet, VGG16_bn, VGG19_bn, ResNet18/34/50) were trained on retrospective CT data and compared, with GoogLeNet performing best, intended to help screen for PCD, a cause of otitis media that is easy to miss clinically.
emb:L2019706419.dataset_size: 31 children with PCD, 30 age-matched children with OME
emb:L2019706419.headline_result: GoogLeNet model accuracy of 0.99 for PCD screening

emb:L2020245090.clinical_problem: developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) detection and classification
emb:L2020245090.patient_population: infants with clinical suspicion of DDH, mean age 87 days (range 4-267 days), at two tertiary pediatric hospitals (Edmonton, Canada and Melbourne, Australia)
emb:L2020245090.model_description: Analyzes 3D ultrasound of the infant hip and automatically calculates two standard DDH indices (alpha angle and femoral head coverage) without user input, classifying each hip as normal or dysplastic. The commercial, FDA-cleared algorithm, trained on data from one site, was tested retrospectively on hips from that site and an independent site it had not seen before, and compared against conventional clinical diagnosis made from concurrent 2D ultrasound.
emb:L2020245090.dataset_size: 2,492 hips from 1,563 patients (1,294 hips Edmonton, 1,198 hips Melbourne)
emb:L2020245090.headline_result: Sensitivity 0.90 for dysplasia; correctly categorized 90% (148/165) of dysplastic hips and 86% (2,006/2,327) of other hips; kappa = 0.79 agreement with clinical diagnosis

emb:L2020890650.model_family: convolutional neural network (CNN) approaches for image segmentation
emb:L2020890650.clinical_problem: evaluating fetal brain development in the second and third trimester via MRI
emb:L2020890650.patient_population: fetuses in the second and third trimester of pregnancy
emb:L2020890650.model_description: A review summarizing the use of convolutional neural networks, the most common deep-learning approach for medical image segmentation, to improve fetal brain MRI quality and analyze fetal brain development in the second and third trimesters, noting that motion-related image degradation limits fetal MRI and that CNN-based segmentation, though mature in adult applications, remains at an early stage for fetal imaging.

emb:L2021327135.model_family: low-light image enhancement stacked with a dense convolutional network (DenseNet) classifier
emb:L2021327135.clinical_problem: detection of fetal heart defects on fetal echocardiography
emb:L2021327135.patient_population: fetuses undergoing fetal echocardiography (460 ultrasound images used to develop the enhancement model)
emb:L2021327135.model_description: FetalNet first enhances low-light, low-contrast fetal echocardiography ultrasound images, then feeds the enhanced images into a dense convolutional network classifier to predict the presence of a fetal heart defect. Developed and evaluated using 460 ultrasound images, with enhancement quality measured by peak signal-to-noise ratio, structural similarity and mean squared error, and detection performance measured on unseen data.
emb:L2021327135.headline_result: Image enhancement: PSNR 30.85 dB, SSIM 0.96, MSE 18.16; FHD prediction rate improved ~25% in accuracy/sensitivity/specificity, 100% predictive negative on unseen data

emb:L2021371208.model_family: gray-scale ultrasound radiomics with LASSO feature selection and logistic regression
emb:L2021371208.clinical_problem: differentiating subcutaneous hemangioma from Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma (KHE)
emb:L2021371208.patient_population: 252 lesions from 143 children with subcutaneous hemangioma and 70 children with KHE
emb:L2021371208.model_description: Extracts gray-scale ultrasound radiomics features from 252 lesions in 213 children with subcutaneous hemangioma or Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma, selects 22 stable features with LASSO, and builds logistic-regression radiomics models (alone and combined with clinical data) to differentiate the two entities, which require different management.
emb:L2021371208.dataset_size: 252 lesions from 213 children (143 with hemangioma, 70 with KHE); 176 training / 76 validation
emb:L2021371208.headline_result: Combined clinical-radiomics model AUC 0.90 (95% CI 0.88-0.92) in the validation set, higher than the radiomics-only model (AUC 0.85)

emb:L2021408484.clinical_problem: detection of atrial septal defect, a congenital heart disease
emb:L2021408484.patient_population: patients with atrial septal defect, a congenital heart disease often asymptomatic through childhood/youth
emb:L2021408484.model_description: A review discussing atrial septal defect, a congenital heart disease often asymptomatic through youth, and surveying deep learning algorithms applied across the imaging and diagnostic modalities used to identify it, including echocardiography, chest radiography, MRI and CT, summarizing the strengths and limitations of each approach.

emb:L2021414987.exclusion_reason: chest X-ray pneumonia classifier; pediatric mortality is cited only as background motivation and the dataset's pediatric status is not stated in the abstract

emb:L2027620303.clinical_problem: prenatal diagnostic ultrasound: fetal CNS examination, fetal cardiac anatomy assessment, quantification of cardiac function
emb:L2027620303.model_description: A review describing how AI-assisted automated segmentation of 2D and 3D ultrasound images is being integrated into prenatal diagnostic workflow, assisting targeted examination of the fetal central nervous system and cardiac anatomy and the quantification of cardiac functional parameters, and discussing requirements for clinical implementation including trained staff.

emb:L2016104415.exclusion_reason: radiomics model predicts a maternal condition (placenta accreta spectrum) in pregnant women; not a fetal or pediatric patient population

emb:L2018702597.model_family: deep learning image reconstruction algorithm, compared against filtered back projection and adaptive statistical iterative reconstruction (ASIR-V)
emb:L2018702597.clinical_problem: assessing vessel wall thickening in pediatric Takayasu arteritis on low-dose CT
emb:L2018702597.patient_population: 32 children with Takayasu arteritis undergoing low-dose contrast-enhanced CT at Beijing Children's Hospital
emb:L2018702597.model_description: Applies a deep learning image reconstruction (DLIR) algorithm to low-dose contrast-enhanced CT scans in children with Takayasu arteritis, comparing image quality and vessel wall thickness measurement accuracy against filtered back projection and two levels of adaptive statistical iterative reconstruction (ASIR-V). DLIR improved vessel wall identification and diagnostic confidence and reduced measurement variability compared with the other reconstruction methods, potentially allowing further radiation dose reduction.
emb:L2018702597.headline_result: DLIR reduced the coefficient of variation of vessel wall thickness measurement by 22.9% and increased contrast-to-noise ratio by 46.8% compared with 50%ASIR-V
emb:L2018702597.study_design: retrospective single-center image quality / measurement accuracy study

emb:L2016436618.clinical_problem: improving through-plane resolution of diffusion MRI in the developing brain
emb:L2016436618.patient_population: preterm newborns from the developing Human Connectome Project; framework also tested on fetal data
emb:L2016436618.model_description: Trains an unsupervised autoencoder neural network to enhance the through-plane resolution of diffusion-weighted MRI in preterm newborns from the developing Human Connectome Project, and to replace motion-corrupted slice outliers, outperforming conventional linear/cubic interpolation on both the diffusion signal and derived diffusion tensor maps. The same network generalized qualitatively to fetal brain data with varying degrees of motion and also acted as a denoiser.

emb:L2016370572.model_description: Compares different MRI sequence inputs (Dixon water, fat and T2* images versus low-resolution T2-weighted anatomical scans) for training 3D U-Net convolutional neural networks to segment the liver and compute liver volume in adolescents with obesity, using whole-liver manual segmentation as reference. The model trained on Dixon water and fat images performed best, while models using only T2-weighted anatomical images performed slightly worse but remained acceptable for longitudinal pediatric obesity studies.
emb:L2016370572.headline_result: Best model (water+fat images): Dice similarity coefficient 0.94, normalized root mean square error 4.2% for liver volume

emb:L2016436171.model_family: geometric deep learning models (graph/mesh/spherical CNNs) benchmarked against traditional Euclidean deep learning
emb:L2016436171.clinical_problem: neonatal cortical surface segmentation and prediction of postmenstrual age at scan / gestational age at birth
emb:L2016436171.patient_population: neonates from the developing Human Connectome Project (dHCP)
emb:L2016436171.model_description: Benchmarks a range of geometric deep learning models, which operate on graphs, meshes and surfaces, against traditional Euclidean CNNs on two tasks using sphericalized neonatal cortical surface MRI data from the dHCP: predicting postmenstrual age at scan and gestational age at birth, and segmenting the cortical surface into anatomical regions per the M-CRIB-S atlas. Performance is assessed by accuracy as well as dependence on image registration and interpretability via occlusion analysis.
emb:L2016436171.release_evidence: The code, and instructions for data access, are available from https://github.com/Abdulah-Fawaz/Benchmarking-Surface-DL
emb:L2016436171.dataset_size: developing Human Connectome Project neonatal cortical surface dataset

emb:L2015898396.model_family: benchmark of 21 machine learning algorithms (parametric, nonparametric, Bayesian, linear/nonlinear, tree-based, kernel-based); best performers Extreme Gradient Boosting, Random Forest Regression, Support Vector Regression with RBF kernel
emb:L2015898396.clinical_problem: brain-age prediction from structural MRI as a biomarker of brain maturation
emb:L2015898396.patient_population: 2,105 typically developing individuals aged 5-22 years from five cohorts; tested on 4,078 pre-adolescents aged 9-10 and 594 individuals aged 5-21
emb:L2015898396.model_description: Trains and systematically compares 21 machine learning algorithms for predicting an individual's age (brain-age) from structural MRI features in 2,105 typically developing youths aged 5-22 from five cohorts, then tests the trained models in two independent holdout datasets. Evaluates both accuracy (mean absolute error) and computational efficiency, and examines the effect of parcellation scheme, number of imaging features, cross-validation folds, outliers, and sample size.
emb:L2015898396.dataset_size: 2,105 training individuals from five cohorts; 4,078 and 594 individuals in two independent holdout test sets
emb:L2015898396.headline_result: Best algorithms: Extreme Gradient Boosting (MAE 1.49), Random Forest Regression (MAE 1.58), Support Vector Regression with RBF kernel (MAE 1.64)

emb:L2015873622.model_family: neural network trained on blind ultrasound sweep video ("cineloops")
emb:L2015873622.clinical_problem: gestational age estimation without standard fetal biometry
emb:L2015873622.patient_population: 4,695 pregnant volunteers in North Carolina (USA) and Zambia
emb:L2015873622.model_description: Trains a neural network on blind ultrasound sweeps of the gravid abdomen, obtained without a trained sonographer targeting specific fetal structures, to estimate gestational age. Compares the model's accuracy against standard fetal biometry performed by trained sonographers across multiple test sets, including data collected by untrained users with low-cost battery-powered ultrasound devices, aiming to expand access to gestational dating in low-resource settings.
emb:L2015873622.headline_result: Model mean absolute error 3.9 days vs. 4.7 days for standard biometry (difference -0.8 days, 95% CI -1.1 to -0.5, p<0.001)

emb:L2015873901.exclusion_reason: fMRI-based prediction of irritability from task-induced brain network reconfiguration; behavioral-trait neuroscience research, not a diagnostic radiology application

emb:L2015549032.exclusion_reason: canonical-correlation analysis linking resting-state functional connectome to cognition/psychopathology dimensions; basic neuroscience research, not a diagnostic radiology application

emb:L2012510433.exclusion_reason: chest X-ray pneumonia classifier; pediatric mortality is cited only as background motivation and the dataset's pediatric status is not stated in the abstract

emb:L2014069118.clinical_problem: AI applications in obstetric and gynecologic ultrasound, including fetal biometry, ovarian tumor malignancy assessment, and fetal CNS/cardiac evaluation
emb:L2014069118.patient_population: fetuses; patients undergoing obstetric and gynecologic ultrasound
emb:L2014069118.model_description: A review of AI, particularly deep learning with convolutional neural networks, applied to ultrasound in obstetrics and gynecology: identifying body parts and computing estimated fetal weight from fetal ultrasound movies, assessing ovarian tumor malignancy comparably to expert scoring systems, and early application to the fetal central nervous system and fetal heart, an area still in early development relative to more mature modalities such as CT and MRI.

emb:L2014069119.clinical_problem: objective assessment of fetal facial expressions as a marker of fetal brain function and neurodevelopment
emb:L2014069119.patient_population: fetuses in the latter half of pregnancy
emb:L2014069119.model_description: A review discussing how artificial intelligence, particularly deep learning, can enable objective, automated recognition of fetal facial expressions on four-dimensional ultrasound, moving beyond prior subjective visual assessment, as a potential window into fetal brain function and neurobehavioral development.

emb:L2015042740.model_family: 3D CNN-based localization and landmark-guided pose estimation with deformable slice-to-volume registration (DSVR)
emb:L2015042740.clinical_problem: reconstructing high-resolution 3D fetal thorax MRI from motion-corrupted scans to support diagnosis of congenital heart and body anomalies
emb:L2015042740.model_description: A fully automated pipeline that uses a 3D convolutional neural network to localize the fetal trunk within motion-corrupted, multi-stack T2-weighted fetal MRI and estimate its pose, then reconstructs a high-resolution 3D image of the fetal thorax in a standard radiological/atlas space using deformable slice-to-volume registration, automatically excluding stacks affected by low image quality or severe motion. Evaluated on fetal MRI datasets spanning 21-36 weeks' gestational age and simulated motion, including assessment of vascular structure definition.
emb:L2015042740.dataset_size: 100 MRI datasets across 21-36 weeks gestational age

emb:L2014578282.model_family: radiomics with Boruta feature selection and random forest
emb:L2014578282.clinical_problem: predicting the molecular subgroup of pediatric medulloblastoma preoperatively
emb:L2014578282.patient_population: 100 children with primary medulloblastoma (First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University, 2011-2020)
emb:L2014578282.model_description: Extracts 5,929 three-dimensional radiomic features from manually delineated tumor regions on multi-sequence MRI in 100 children with medulloblastoma, selects stable features with the Boruta algorithm, and builds a random forest model, alone and combined with clinical features, to predict the tumor's molecular subgroup (WNT, SHH, Group3, Group4), which currently requires molecular/genetic testing, in order to support earlier individualized treatment planning.
emb:L2014578282.headline_result: Combined clinical-radiomic model AUC 0.944 for WNT and 0.819 for SHH subgroup in the testing cohort (radiomics-only model AUC 0.519 for Group3, 0.705 for Group4)

emb:L2013825173.model_family: VGG-16-based deep learning architecture combined with a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network
emb:L2013825173.clinical_problem: assessing inferior vena cava collapse to guide intravenous fluid resuscitation in dehydrated children
emb:L2013825173.patient_population: pediatric patients presenting to a pediatric emergency department with dehydration (184 IVC ultrasound videos)
emb:L2013825173.model_description: A VGG-16-based deep learning model, run inside a Long Short-Term Memory architecture, analyzes real-time point-of-care ultrasound video of the inferior vena cava to classify complete versus incomplete IVC collapse in children being evaluated for intravenous fluid resuscitation. Trained and tested on 184 previously acquired, de-identified pediatric emergency department ultrasound videos (166 for training/validation, 18 held out for testing), and compared against two blinded point-of-care ultrasound experts.
emb:L2013825173.dataset_size: 184 patient IVC ultrasound videos (166 training/validation, 18 held-out test)
emb:L2013825173.headline_result: Substantial agreement with the PEM POCUS attending (Cohen's kappa 0.78, 95% CI 0.49-1.0) and with the PEM resident (kappa 0.66, 95% CI 0.31-1.0) on held-out test videos

emb:L2014145795.exclusion_reason: erratum/correction notice listing conflict-of-interest statements for unrelated prior publications; not a research study

emb:L2014200603.model_family: 3D deep convolutional neural network built on U-Net with dense connections and residual skip-connections
emb:L2014200603.clinical_problem: brain tissue segmentation (white matter, gray matter, cerebrospinal fluid)
emb:L2014200603.patient_population: IBSR18 dataset (diverse age groups) and iSeg-2017 multi-modality challenge dataset (MRI scans of infants)
emb:L2014200603.model_description: A compact 3D deep convolutional network built on the U-Net architecture, using densely connected convolutional layers and residual skip-connections, to segment brain MRI into white matter, gray matter and cerebrospinal fluid while using far fewer parameters (40-98% fewer) than comparable deep-learning architectures. Trained with cross-entropy, Dice, and combined loss functions and evaluated on the IBSR18 dataset and the iSeg-2017 infant brain segmentation challenge dataset, intended to support study of brain structure/development, detection of abnormal tissue, diagnosis, and surgical guidance.
emb:L2014200603.headline_result: Best performance on the IBSR18 test set and competitive performance on the iSeg-2017 infant challenge dataset, while reducing parameters by 40-98% versus comparable architectures
